questions.text:
Consider the following four processes with arrival times (in milliseconds) and their length of CPU burst (in milliseconds) as shown below:
These processes are run on a single processor using preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First scheduling algorithm. If the average waiting time of the processes is 1 millisecond, then the value of Z is __________.
questions.solution:
Average waiting time 1 ms [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] total waiting time = 4 ms.

SRTF up to t = 4: P1 runs 0-1; P2 (burst 1) preempts and runs 1-2; P1 runs 2-4 and finishes. P1 waited 1, P2 waited 0.

At t = 4, P3 (3 ms, arrived at 3) and P4 (Z) are left. For the total to be 4, they must wait 3 in total.
With Z = 2: P4 runs 4-6 (wait 0), P3 runs 6-9 (wait 9 [latex]-[/latex] 3 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 3). Total = 1 + 0 + 3 + 0 = 4 True

Answer: 2

questions.text: The index node (inode) of a Unix-like file system has 12 direct, one single-indirect and one double-indirect pointer The disk block size is 4 kB and the disk block addresses 32-bits long. The maximum possible file size is (rounded off to 1 decimal place) __________ GB.
questions.solution:
Pointers per block = 4 KB / 4 B = 1024.
- Direct: 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 48 KB
- Single indirect: 1024 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4 MB
- Double indirect: [latex]1024^2[/latex] [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4 GB

Total [latex]\approx[/latex] 4 GB + 4 MB + 48 KB [latex]\approx[/latex] 4.0 GB

Answer: 4.0

questions.text:
Consider the augmented grammar given below:
[latex]S'\rightarrow S[/latex]
[latex]S \rightarrow \lt L \gt |id[/latex]
[latex]L \rightarrow L,S|S[/latex]

Let [latex]I_0=CLOSURE(\{[S'\rightarrow \cdot S]\}) [/latex]. The number of items in the set [latex]GOTO(I_0,\lt)[/latex] is __________.
questions.solution:
In [latex]I_0[/latex], the item [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot\lt L\gt[/latex] moves on [latex]\lt[/latex] to [latex]S\rightarrow\lt\cdot L\gt[/latex]. Closure (dot before L, then before S):
1. [latex]S\rightarrow\lt\cdot L\gt[/latex]
2. [latex]L\rightarrow\cdot L,S[/latex]
3. [latex]L\rightarrow\cdot S[/latex]
4. [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot\lt L\gt[/latex]
5. [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot id[/latex]

Answer: 5

questions.text:
Consider the following matrix:
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 4 & 8\\ 1& 3 & 9 &27 \\ 1 & 4 & 16 &64 \\ 1 & 5 & 25 &125 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
The absolute value of the product of Eigenvalues of R is _________ .
questions.solution:
Product of eigenvalues = determinant. The matrix is a Vandermonde matrix with values 2, 3, 4, 5:
[latex]\det=\prod_{i \lt j}(x_j-x_i)=(3-2)(4-2)(5-2)(4-3)(5-3)(5-4)=1\cdot2\cdot3\cdot1\cdot2\cdot1=12[/latex]

Answer: 12

questions.text: A certain processor deploys a single-level cache. The cache block size is 8 words and the word size is 4 bytes. The memory system uses a 60-MHz clock. To service a cache-miss, the memory controller first takes 1 cycle to accept the starting address of the block, it then takes 3 cycles to fetch all the eight words of the block, and finally transmits the words of the requested block at the rate of 1 word per cycle. The maximum bandwidth for the memory system when the program running on the processor issues a series of read operations is _________[latex]\times 10^6[/latex] bytes/sec.
questions.solution:
One cache miss brings one block of 8 words [latex]\times[/latex] 4 bytes = 32 bytes.
Cycles per block = 1 (address) + 3 (fetch) + 8 (transfer, 1 word per cycle) = 12 cycles.

Time per block = 12 / 60 MHz = 0.2 [latex]\mu[/latex]s.
Bandwidth = 32 bytes / 0.2 [latex]\mu[/latex]s = [latex]160\times10^6[/latex] bytes/s

Answer: 160
